## The spec (this is a self-contained bug-fix PR; the PR body IS the spec)
The integer geohash decode path (`decode_int` / `decode_bbox_int` / `neighbor_int` / `neighbors_int` / `bboxes_int`) silently returns a WRONG latitude for every ODD `bitDepth`, while the string path (`decode`/`decode_bbox`) is correct. The PR's goal: make odd bitDepth correct while leaving even bitDepth byte-for-byte identical, WITHOUT adding a validation/throw on odd bitDepth.

Root cause stated in spec: `decode_bbox_int` used `step = bitDepth/2` and one loop reading one lon + one lat bit per iteration; for odd bitDepth the loop ran an extra iteration whose latitude bit position `((step-i)*2)-2` went NEGATIVE, and `get_bit(bits,-1)` always returns 0, halving `maxLat` once too many, collapsing the latitude bbox to half height.

Stated fix: geohash interleaves bits longitude-first, so bitDepth bd has ceil(bd/2) longitude bits and floor(bd/2) latitude bits; read the two axes in SEPARATE loops with non-negative bit positions. `encode_int` is already symmetric for odd bitDepth and needs no change. `decode_int`/`neighbor_int`/`neighbors_int`/`bboxes_int` are fixed transitively.
